comparison: Both strongly support the core experimental finding that dopamine ramps depend on ITI duration and dynamic cues. OpenEval emphasizes converging evidence from simulations and experiments (C2, C17-C23), while peer reviewers focus on the rapid appearance/disappearance of ramps (C2, C21-C24) and call this the 'clearest demonstration to date.' Both evaluations are SUPPORTED with high confidence.

Both support the behavioral control analysis showing dopamine ramps are independent of behavioral differences. OpenEval emphasizes the counterbalanced design (C24-C25), while peer reviewers explicitly note 'licking behavior was similar on different trial types and was not related to ramping activity' (C25, C55-C56). Both are SUPPORTED.

Perfect agreement on trial-by-trial adaptation evidence (C26-C31). Both evaluations support the rapid adaptation of eligibility trace time constant to ITI changes. OpenEval provides detailed statistical assessment, while peer reviewers accept these analyses as part of 'well done and thoughtfully presented' studies. Both are SUPPORTED.

Both support the generalization to instrumental conditioning (C32-C37). OpenEval notes the replication strengthens conclusions despite more gradual dynamics, while peer reviewers accept the extension across tasks without challenge. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Overlapping support for basic behavioral learning (C32-C33, C17). Both evaluations accept that animals learned the tasks successfully across conditions, establishing the context for dopamine findings. Both are SUPPORTED.

Perfect agreement on the ANCCR theoretical framework (C38, C64-C68, C71-C72). Both evaluations support the model's mechanistic explanation and its value for the field. Peer reviewers emphasize the work is 'potentially highly impactful' and provides 'important constraint for models,' while OpenEval notes the parsimonious account is well-supported. Both are SUPPORTED.

Both support the contextualization within prior literature (C39-C42). OpenEval notes appropriate citations and honest acknowledgment of inconsistencies, while peer reviewers accept the literature review without challenge. Both are SUPPORTED.

Both rate speculative explanations as UNCERTAIN (C45-C47). OpenEval explicitly notes these are 'appropriately qualified' but 'remain hypothetical,' while peer reviewers' silence on these claims suggests neither strong support nor challenge. Both evaluations are UNCERTAIN.

Both support the necessity of dynamic cues (C48). OpenEval emphasizes the experimental evidence directly supports this requirement, while peer reviewers accept this as an established constraint. Both are SUPPORTED.

Divergent evaluations of interpretive claims about ANCCR applications (C49-C52). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting reasonable inferences and appropriate distinction between findings and speculation. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, neither supporting nor challenging these extensions. OpenEval is more confident in the reasonableness of these interpretations.

Both support the critical analysis of alternative models (C53-C63). OpenEval notes the well-reasoned argument that ANCCR provides more principled explanations, while peer reviewers implicitly accept this through positive assessments of theoretical contribution. Both are SUPPORTED.

Perfect agreement on UNCERTAIN evaluation of simulation discrepancy (C69-C70). Both note the authors honestly identify the limitation and offer speculative explanation. OpenEval emphasizes appropriate transparency, while peer reviewers do not explicitly address it. Both are UNCERTAIN.

Perfect agreement on methodological rigor (C73-C87). OpenEval provides detailed assessment noting appropriate sample sizes and procedures, while peer reviewers explicitly state 'these studies are well done and thoughtfully presented.' Both are SUPPORTED.

Perfect agreement on field characterization (C1, C3-C9). Both support the description of classical views, recent findings, and theoretical controversies. OpenEval notes appropriate citations, while peer reviewers accept the framing of ramping dopamine as part of 'recent theoretical and computational debates.' Both are SUPPORTED.

Perfect agreement on ANCCR framework description (C10-C16). Both support the theoretical principles and prior predictions as appropriate motivation. OpenEval emphasizes clear statement with citations, while peer reviewers accept the framework as basis for experimental predictions. Both are SUPPORTED.

Both support ANCCR simulations (C18-C19) as providing valid framework for experimental predictions. OpenEval includes these in broader assessment of converging evidence, while peer reviewers separately affirm the simulations. Both are SUPPORTED.

Partial overlap on ITI-dopamine relationship. OpenEval's R1 includes C20 as part of experimental evidence for main finding, while peer R2 specifically addresses the correlation between ITI duration and ramp strength (C20, C34). Both are SUPPORTED.

Overlapping coverage of inconsistency with prior literature (C43-C44). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting honest acknowledgment and appropriate qualification. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, not explicitly addressing the discrepancy or speculative explanations. OpenEval is more confident in the appropriateness of how this is handled.
